historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 company guidance midpoint (total income NZ$128-134m vs FY2026 NZ$120.9m = +8.4%), reaffirmed 29-Jul-2026 with no subsequent revision as at 26-Sep-2026; used as the year-1 driver in place of any historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is NEGATIVE (-11.0% 3yr, -2.9% 5yr) because the company funds losses out of equity raised in 2018-2022 -- book value is being consumed, not compounded. EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined: EPS is negative in every year except FY2018-19, and owner FCF is negative in all ten years. Revenue CAGR (+37% 3yr) diverges from equity CAGR by far more than 30%, which is the point: revenue growth is real but has never converted into cash or book value. Selected growth rate is therefore taken from company guidance, NOT extrapolated from the revenue CAGR, which would be the single largest error available here.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR is not computable -- the SBC/interest/lease-adjusted FCF series is negative in every one of FY2017-FY2026 (-2.91, 0.13, -4.57, -18.30, -30.30, -40.34, -46.33, -15.84, -11.45, -13.02). Only FY2018 is positive, at NZ$0.13m. FY2026 owner FCF (-13.02m) WIDENED from FY2025 (-11.45m) even though reported FCF improved slightly (-2.89m vs -1.40m) -- the improvement is an SBC/growth-in-SBC artefact, not a cash-generation improvement.

scenario_narratives.base: RENEWED, BUT ON WORSE TERMS. Booking.com renews in 2029 because the relationship works for both sides, but prices it to its own advantage -- Serko is non-exclusive and replaceable, and the volume tiers already ratchet the take rate down from ~48.7% toward 40% at 6m room nights. Volume keeps compounding at 15-20%; revenue grows at roughly half that as the take rate erodes, starting from the guided +8.4% in FY2027 when spend exceeds income and operating leverage goes BACKWARDS exactly as management guides. The cost optimisation programme and the roll-off of the FY2022-24 capitalised-development amortisation wave then let margins expand slowly. Owner FCF crosses zero around FY2032 -- two to three years later than management's own FY2029-30 inflection, because management's framing excludes SBC and lease principal. Terminal owner-FCF margin ~5.0%. Equity value is essentially the cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: THE AI OPERATING LAYER LANDS. Serko.ai converts from closed beta into a commercial product with a new pricing model, monetising two decades of proprietary corporate booking behaviour and supplier connectivity that a generic LLM wrapper cannot synthesise. The US corporate wedge -- management sizes USD$16-24bn of accommodation spend in the target industries -- converts well beyond the two customers signed to date, feeding volume into the Booking.com engine Serko already operates. Booking.com renews on acceptable terms because Serko has become harder to replace. Revenue compounds mid-to-high teens toward the NZ$250m FY2030 aspiration, and the cost-optimisation programme delivers real operating leverage to a 27.5% EBITDA margin.
scenario_narratives.bear: THE BOOKING.COM CLIFF. The contract expires 31 March 2029 and is terminable on 12 months' notice by either side, so notice could be served as early as FY2028. Booking Holdings in-sources the SME business-travel layer it already brands as its own. Supplier commissions, 61% of revenue, run off through FY2030 (modelled as a 45% revenue collapse in that year). What remains is Zeno in Australasia -- entrenched but mature -- plus a declining GetThere. Serko.ai has no revenue. Owner FCF stays negative throughout and terminal value hits the zero floor; equity value is negative.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Revenue x normalizing owner-FCF-margin DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, component-built, probability-weighted across three scenarios. THIS IS EXPLICITLY NOT A TRAILING-FCF DCF, because Serko has no trailing FCF to discount: on the house owner-FCF basis (reported FCF less SBC, less interest income, less IFRS-16 lease principal) the company generated NEGATIVE free cash flow in ALL TEN years FY2017-FY2026, and FY2026 owner FCF (-NZ$13.02m, -10.9% of revenue) WIDENED from FY2025. Growing a negative base by any positive rate produces a more negative number; growing it by a negative rate produces a spurious positive. Neither is a valuation. Value is instead built from the one line that is genuinely compounding -- revenue, up NZ$46.5m -> 68.8 -> 88.5 -> 119.4m over FY2023-26 -- multiplied by a cash margin allowed to normalise over an explicit ten-year path, with every component (EBITDA margin, SBC, D&A, tax, capex, working capital, lease cost) modelled separately. The central question: Serko is a growth company approaching breakeven whose largest revenue stream is contractually programmed to become LESS profitable as it grows -- the Booking.com revenue share steps down with volume (roughly 50% below 4.3m completed room nights, ~40% blended at 6m, ~32% at 8.6m), and Serko hit 4.3m in FY2026, permanently exiting the top tier. Q1 FY2027 is the proof: room nights +39%, revenue per room night -11%. The Booking.com contract expiry (31-Mar-2029, inside the forecast horizon, terminable for convenience on 12 months' notice, non-exclusive) is handled as an explicit dated event in the cash flows rather than buried in a discount-rate premium: BEAR (35%) assumes non-renewal/material repricing with a 45% FY2030 revenue collapse as the 61% supplier-commissions line runs off; BASE (45%) assumes renewal on worse economics; BULL (20%) assumes renewal on acceptable terms plus Serko.ai and the US wedge landing. As at 26-Sep-2026 the underlying facts are unchanged from the 28-Aug-2026 build -- only price (NZ$1.465 -> NZ$1.33, a fresh 52-week low reached on no company-specific news) and the confirmed share count (124.882m -> 126.139m per the 22-Sep Capital Change Notice) have moved.
key_risks_to_valuation: Booking.com contract: 61% of revenue, expires 31-Mar-2029, 12-month mutual termination for convenience, NON-EXCLUSIVE, take rate steps down with volume.
Customer concentration: two customers = 71% of FY2026 revenue (NZ$84.9m of 119.4m).
Ten consecutive years of negative owner FCF; breakeven pushed out to FY2029-FY2030 by management.
FY2027 guided spend (NZ$132-140m) EXCEEDS guided income (NZ$128-134m) at every point -- operating leverage reverses; reaffirmed 29-Jul-2026, no update since.
Management missed 3 of 5 FY2026 scorecard KPIs: B4B CRN threshold, platform capabilities, North American contracted ARR.
AI disintermediation risk sharpening: Navan's 'AI room intelligence mapper' and SAP Concur's Joule AI agents both sit in the same booking/content layer Serko occupies (trade press, Sep-2026).
SBC of NZ$7.246m exceeds EBITDAFI of NZ$6.5m -- the headline profit metric is smaller than the equity cost it ignores.

Continued share-price de-rating to fresh 52-week lows through Sep-2026 on no adverse company-specific news, widening the gap to sell-side consensus (~NZ$3.10-3.44) to over 130% -- a market that has stopped crediting the Serko 2030 aspiration, not a single dislocation.

inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD flows discounted at an NZD-built rate. Serko has zero interest-bearing debt so WACC = cost of equity. Build-up: NZ 10yr risk-free 4.5% + ERP 6.0% x beta ~1.5 (unprofitable small-cap tech) = 9.0% + small-cap illiquidity premium 2.0% (market cap now ~NZ$150-165m, thin NZX/ASX dual-listed liquidity) + loss-making-with-no-proven-path-to-profit premium 1.5% (10 consecutive years of negative owner FCF; management pushed the inflection to FY2029-FY2030) + EUR/NZD structural mismatch 0.5% (costs in NZD, ~63% of revenue invoiced through the Netherlands Booking.com entity in EUR; only EUR32.0m of FY2027 hedged) = 17.5% total. Customer concentration and the Booking.com contract expiry are deliberately NOT charged in the discount rate -- they are modelled explicitly as a FY2030 non-renewal event in the bear-case cash flows (35% weight) to avoid double-counting the same risk in both the rate and the flows. Robustness: base-case drivers held fixed, IV is NZ$0.77 at an implausible 10% WACC, NZ$0.65 at 12%, NZ$0.49 at 15% -- the valuation gap to the NZ$1.33 market price is driven by the cash-flow path, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B: IFRS-16 lease principal (NZ$1.344m FY2026, ~1.1% of revenue) deducted inside the flows as an operating cost via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (NZ$6.934m) therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Charged once, never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- Serko has no non-controlling interests; GetThere and the Booking.com arrangement are both wholly owned/contractual, not part-owned subsidiaries.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 35% bear / 45% base / 20% bull -- materially more bearish than the 15/50/35 house default, and deliberately so. BEAR raised to 35% because the Booking.com contract (61% of revenue, 71% concentration with one other customer) expires 31-Mar-2029 INSIDE the forecast window, is terminable by either side on 12 months' notice, and is NON-EXCLUSIVE -- so an adverse outcome is a specifically-dated contractual event, not a tail risk. Management also missed three of five FY2026 scorecard KPIs, including the B4B CRN threshold and North American contracted ARR. Unchanged from the prior build: the 26-Sep-2026 Analysis.json refresh finds no new disclosure on Booking.com renewal terms, and confirms the same commission-tier mechanics (Q1 FY2027: CRNs +39%, ARPCRN -11%). BULL held at 20% because it still requires three independent things to go right at once: Serko.ai commercialising from closed beta (open beta not due until Q3 FY2027, still zero revenue as at Sep-2026), the US corporate wedge converting beyond the two customers signed to date, AND Booking.com renewing on acceptable terms. BASE at 45% is the residual: contract renewed but on worse economics, consistent with the take-rate step-down already visible in the data.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
